question: In what different ways can the expressing aspect of a word appear?
premises: The expressing aspect of a word does not appear in only one fixed mode.
Sometimes it appears with the expressed absorbed into its own nature.
Sometimes it appears as expressing only a general flash of meaning.
inference: The expressing aspect of speech appears in varying modes, either absorbing the expressed into itself or presenting only a general meaning.
plain_english: Sometimes the expressing aspect appears with the expressed absorbed into its own nature; sometimes, instead, it appears as expressing a general flash.
